description: The portfolio's Renovate configuration lives in sborka and is extended by name. What was here before was `config:recommended` and nothing else, and #157 and #158 are what that costs: one sborka release, 0.2.0.30, as two pull requests. The version is named in settings.gradle.kts and again in the catalog, and only a grouping rule makes them one change.

sborka's `automerge-harness` is extended second, so `github-actions` and `gradle-wrapper` updates merge themselves on green — with the exception below. The precondition holds, re-checked 2026-11-25: `check.yml` runs on every `pull_request`. This file used to say `publish.yml` runs on every push to `main`; it now runs on a tag, and `dockerhub.yaml` only by hand, and the docker actions they use are used by no pull request — those wait for a person.

The actions that only `publish.yml` (a tag) and `dockerhub.yaml` (by hand) uses wait for a person: that workflow runs on a tag (or by hand), no pull request runs it, so a green pull request says nothing about them and a broken one would surface at the next release, not on the merge. Every other action and the wrapper merge themselves through `automerge-harness`, because the pull-request workflows ran exactly those versions.

AFTER the presets, because the last match wins, and in a group of its own: Renovate merges a grouped pull request only when every update in it may merge, so left in `ci actions` these would hold every other action with them. The list is what that workflow uses and no pull-request workflow does (re-checked 2026-11-25); an action added to that workflow later is not on it until somebody adds it here.

customManagers.description: Versions that live in the harness scripts rather than in a manifest Renovate knows: a `# renovate: datasource=… depName=…` comment directly above a `readonly NAME_VERSION=…` line. DuckDB is the first, in ci/consumers.sh — installed by pip inside a container, it was unpinned until 2.0.0 changed its multipart uploader and turned `consumers` red on every pull request with no change to point at.
